chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'ammar ibn Khallad, who said:

I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'For Allah there are servants in the earth who strive regarding the needs of the people; they are the secure ones on the Day of Resurrection. And whoever brings gladness to a believer, Allah will gladden his heart on the Day of Resurrection.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for fulfilling the needs of believers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), emphasizing that proactive service to believers is a defining characteristic of the 'secure' (al-aminun) on the Day of Judgment. This tradition underscores the Shia concept of *ta'awun* (mutual assistance), linking the spiritual tranquility of the servant directly to the relief of the believer's distress, thereby elevating social welfare to an act of worship.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Moammar Bin Khallad who said,

‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘For Allah<sup>azwj</sup> there are servants in the earth striving regarding the needs of the people. They would be secure on the Day of Judgement. And the one who causes the gladness to enter upon a Believer, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Gladden his heart on the Day of Judgement’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Mu’ammar ibn al-Khallad who has said the following: “

I heard abu al-Hassan (a.s.) saying, ‘There are servants of Allah on earth who endeavor to help people, these (helping ones) will be secure and safe on the Day of Judgment. Whoever sends joy to the heart of a believer, on the Day of Judgment, Allah will fill his heart with joy.’”
